details: An order-dependent red gate (30 Oct, branch of first-relay-setup-on-a-new-machine-fails): a test patch of relay_config.ledger_dir stays bound inside relay_ledger for the rest of the process; the branch shielded one victim test, the cause stays. A flaky test is a bug (quality-gate rule).
failing_case: Gate of 47efc720 (this branch): library tests FAILED in
test_hook_ledger.Ledger.test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day, and inert went red because the
probe run passed it: an order-dependent failure. relay_ledger does `from relay_config import claude_json, ledger_dir`
(lib/relay_ledger.py:24), so if relay_ledger is first imported while a test has relay_config.ledger_dir patched
(tests/test_metrics.py:138 is the only such patch), the module keeps that mock for the rest of the process. cfbde7a6
patches mod.relay_ledger.ledger_dir in the one failing test; any other test reading relay_ledger after it (for example
tests/test_transcripts_analysis.py:221 rl.ledger_dir()) still sees the stale folder.
Expected: no test leaves relay_ledger bound to another test's folder; the order of tests does not change a result.
pass_cases: 1. Run test_metrics then test_hook_ledger in one process (parallel_unittest with one worker, or unittest with both
modules): test_has_start... passes without the victim-side patch.
2. Same with test_metrics then test_transcripts_analysis: rl.ledger_dir() is under that test's RELAY_HOME.
3. relay_ledger.ledger_dir() in a fresh process still follows RELAY_HOME (the hook writes to $RELAY_HOME/ledger).
reason: tests/test_metrics.py::Records::test_a_fresh_import_of_relay_ledger_inside_a_records_test_binds_the_real_ledger_dir fails with the old patch, passes now.
findings.summary: A test leaves relay_ledger bound to a patched ledger_dir…

details: CONFIRMED by reproduction (mechanism) with a one-line dropper test from the scratchpad; with the real dropper tests I
tried as the first test (test_roles, test_rules, test_spec_steps, test_numbers_hermetic, test_bench) each re-imported a
real relay_ledger before Records ran, so a red order from today's suite alone is PLAUSIBLE, not shown. Six test files
delete relay_* from sys.modules and the parallel runner splits by class, so which one runs right before a Records test
in a process is not fixed.
The change fixes the order of first import, not the cause (principle 6): relay_ledger binds ledger_dir by name, and
Records patches the attribute of relay_config while code under it may import relay_ledger fresh. The import at the top
of test_metrics only guards the first import of the process; any later re-import under the patch brings the leak back.
The new test reads the name `relay_ledger` in test_metrics' globals, a module object that a drop leaves behind, so it
cannot see a stale module in sys.modules: it passes with the leak present (order B below). Without the fix it fails
only by NameError, not by the mechanism.
evidence: scratchpad/repro/order.py runs the named tests in one process, then prints sys.modules["relay_ledger"].ledger_dir.
victim_nopatch.py = tests/test_hook_ledger.py with the mock.patch.object(mod.relay_ledger, "ledger_dir") lines removed.
A: test_f8 then victim (no drop)                 -> OK
B: dropper_sim, test_f8, new test, victim        -> FAIL: test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day; FAILED (failures=1) (the new test passed)
lib/relay_ledger.py:24    from relay_config import claude_json, ledger_dir
failing_case: One process, in this order: a test that deletes relay_* from sys.modules without putting them back (as
test_numbers_hermetic setUp, test_rules, test_roles, test_spec_steps:535 do), then
Now: f8 runs relay_metrics.front_figures, whose `import relay_analyze` re-imports relay_ledger while relay_config.ledger_dir
is patched; sys.modules["relay_ledger"].ledger_dir stays a MagicMock returning f8's temp ledger folder; the new test
passes (it checks the old module object test_metrics holds by name); the victim FAILS.
Should: the victim passes in every order, and a regression test fails whenever sys.modules["relay_ledger"] is left bound
fix_hint: Remove the patch: in Records.setUp set RELAY_HOME (mock.patch.dict(os.environ, ...)) to a temp home and write the
fixture rows under <home>/ledger, so relay_config.ledger_dir() is the real function and nothing can bind a mock.
Or make lib/relay_ledger.py call relay_config.ledger_dir() through the module (import relay_config) instead of
binding the name. Then make the regression test check sys.modules["relay_ledger"] after a drop and a Records-style
pass_cases: 1. drop relay_* from sys.modules; run Records.test_f8...; then sys.modules["relay_ledger"].ledger_dir() under
RELAY_HOME=<tmp>/home returns <tmp>/home/ledger (today: f8's temp ledger folder).
2. same order, then test_hook_ledger test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day with the victim-side
3. test_metrics then test_hook_ledger (no drop), victim-side patch removed: passes (passes today).
4. Records tests still read the fixture's ledger rows: test_two_riders_get_two_records_and_each_agent_once passes.
5. relay_ledger.ledger_dir() in a fresh process follows RELAY_HOME.
reason: tests/test_metrics.py:142-164: setUp uses RELAY_HOME, so nothing binds a mock; the test pops sys.modules, re-imports, and checks sys.modules and ledger_dir() == self.ledger. Passes, and fails under the old patch. Pass cases 4 and 2/3 pass in the check run.
findings.summary: the leak returns when any earlier test drops relay_* from sys.modules, and the new test still passes then
